turns.content: Can you explain the standard airport traffic pattern?

A standard airport traffic pattern is a rectangular path around the runway, typically flown at 1,000 feet above the airport elevation. Turns are usually made to the left unless otherwise indicated by visual markings.

pairs.context: An airport traffic pattern includes the direction and altitude of the pattern and procedures for entering and leaving the pattern. Unless the airport displays approved visual markings indicating that turns should be made to the right, the pilot should make all turns in the pattern to the left.
